PAPER: CC BY, read from the copyright block printed in the PDF; PDF fetched from https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2016.00196/pdf, 889687 bytes, 5 pages, and archived. DATA: no licence is stated anywhere -- neither the Frontiers data report nor the Neural Engineering Data Consortium downloads page (https://isip.piconepress.com/projects/nedc/html/tuh_eeg/, retrieved 2026-07-31) names a licence or a data use agreement. Access is by completing an Adobe Acrobat form and emailing a signed copy to help@nedcdata.org from a valid institutional address, after which ssh keys and rsync credentials are issued; the form's own terms were not retrieved. md_quality is rough: the two-column Frontiers PDF interleaved column by column with inter-word spacing stripped, and about 25 spurious empty pseudo-tables were inserted where the converter mis-detected the column gutter. Figures 1 and 2 are image-only and lost, which matters: Figure 2 is the sole source for the sessions-per-patient histogram, the sessions-per-calendar-year distribution, the age histogram and the channel-count distribution, so the corpus's year range is not recoverable from the extraction and the card records the conflicting page statements instead. The reference list is column-interleaved and partly unreadable. Two further discrepancies in the source itself are recorded on the card: corpus version v0.6.0 in the body against v0.6.3 in the reference list, and an age standard deviation (55.9) larger than the mean (51.6) on a distribution bounded at 90 years. EXTRACTION UPDATE 2026-08-01 -- source.md was regenerated with pymupdf4llm, which preserves markdown tables and inter-word spacing that the earlier markitdown conversion destroyed, and md_quality was reassessed against the new extraction as clean (was rough).
